summary: Iteration 4 — config-only fix verification for Vercel npm ERESOLVE. Verified /app/frontend/.npmrc exists with exact content 'legacy-peer-deps=true'. package.json unchanged (date-fns@4.1.0 + react-day-picker@8.10.1 still present, no requirements.txt changes). Ran full backend regression (10/10 passing) and frontend smoke on Emergent preview: bottle-scene renders (1440x900 bbox), chapter-hero tagline 'Nature, bottled with reverence.' present, chapter-source visible at y=1260, chapter-people visible at y=3735, cta-order opens order-modal. No regressions from the .npmrc addition.
critical_code_review_comments: .npmrc content is correct: single line 'legacy-peer-deps=true'. This applies to npm and pnpm (yarn v1 ignores it, which is fine since yarn is already lenient). Fix is minimal and non-invasive — package.json + lockfile are untouched so local yarn behavior is preserved.

package.json still declares packageManager 'yarn@1.22.22'. Vercel respects packageManager for corepack; if Vercel is configured to use yarn v1 the .npmrc is a belt-and-suspenders safety net. Recommend main agent confirms Vercel install command / packageManager pickup on next deploy.
No requirements.txt changes; backend behavior unchanged. All 6 SKUs and order endpoints (POST/GET /api/orders) work as before — subtotal/shipping/threshold math intact.
seed_data_creation: None — reused existing TestCreateOrder fixtures which auto-create orders per test.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Iteration 4 is a config-only fix (/app/frontend/.npmrc = 'legacy-peer-deps=true') to unblock Vercel npm ERESOLVE between date-fns@4.1.0 and react-day-picker@8.10.1 (peers ^2||^3). No code paths were changed. Backend suite at /app/backend/tests/backend_test.py fully green. Frontend regression on preview URL confirmed bottle-scene, chapter-hero tagline, chapter-source@y=1260, chapter-people@y=3735, cta-order → order-modal. Deployment-side verification (actual Vercel build) is out of scope for this container.
rca of the issue: Vercel defaults to `npm install` which enforces strict peer-dependency resolution. react-day-picker@8.10.1 declares peerDependencies date-fns '^2.0.0 || ^3.0.0', but the project pins date-fns@4.1.0. npm ERESOLVE aborts with a peer conflict. Locally Emergent uses yarn v1 which is lenient by default. Fix: add /app/frontend/.npmrc with `legacy-peer-deps=true` so npm (and pnpm) skip strict peer resolution and match the yarn behavior, without downgrading date-fns or bumping react-day-picker to v9 (which would be a larger change). Reproduction is outside this container (Vercel-side); mitigation verified by (a) confirming .npmrc content, (b) confirming no other files changed, (c) running full backend + frontend regression on the Emergent preview build.
